Q7406533.label: 1939 Salvadoran presidential election
Q7406533.summary: Presidential elections were held in El Salvador on 21 January 1939. The election was indirect rather than being held through a popular vote. The National Constitutional Assembly elected Brigadier General Maximiliano Hernández Martínez, the incumbent president of El Salvador, to a third presidential term that would last from 1939 to 1945. He was the only candidate and won unopposed.

Q458181.label: 1927 Austrian legislative election
Q458181.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Austria on 24 April 1927. The result was a victory for the Unity List (Einheitsliste), an alliance of the Christian Social Party and the Greater German People's Party, which won 85 of the 165 seats. However this brief coalition failed to result in any larger proportion of the votes than when the CSP ran alone, losing votes to the Landbund. Voter turnout was 89.3%.

Q3931589.label: Italian referendum, 1999
Q3931589.summary: An abrogative referendum on the electoral law was held in Italy on 18 April 1999. Voters were asked whether they approved of replacing the mixed-member proportional representation electoral system with one based solely on single-member constituencies, with the 25% of seats instead allocated to the second-placed in the constituencies with the most votes.

Q552389.label: Spiros Cyprianou
Q552389.desc: 2nd President of the Republic of Cyprus (1977-1988)
Q552389.summary: Spyros Achilleos Kyprianou was a Cypriot barrister and politician, who served as President of Cyprus from 1977 to 1988. He also served as President of the Cypriot House of Representatives from 1976 to 1977 and then again from 1996 to 2001, as well as being President of the Democratic Party, which he founded, from 1976 to 2000.

Q16412101.summary: The 1993 Narva and Sillamäe autonomy referendum was an unconstitutional referendum held on 16–17 July 1993 in Narva and Sillamäe in north-east Estonia, on whether to seek autonomy within the country.

Q53701.label: Axel Pehrsson-Bramstorp
Q53701.summary: Axel Alarik Pehrsson-Bramstorp was a Swedish politician and farmer who served as Prime Minister of Sweden from June to September 1936. Following his premiership, he served as Minister of Agriculture until 1945. Initially a member of the Liberal Coalition Party, Bramstorp served as leader of the Farmers’ League from 1934 and represented Malmö in the Riksdag from 1929 to 1949.

Q367557.label: Thorvald Stauning
Q367557.summary: Thorvald August Marinus Stauning was the first social democratic prime minister of Denmark. He served as prime minister from 1924 to 1926 and again from 1929 until his death in 1942.

Q2053573.label: 1935 Turkish general election
Q2053573.desc: general election held in the Republic of Turkey in 1935
Q2053573.summary: General elections were held in Turkey on 8 February 1935. The Republican People's Party was the only party in the country at the time.

Q66554821.label: 17 August 2019 Kabul bombing
Q66554821.summary: On 17 August 2019, a suicide bombing took place during a wedding in a wedding hall in Kabul, Afghanistan. At least 92 people were killed in the attack and over 140 injured. The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant claimed responsibility for the bombing, stating that the attack targeted the Shi'ites.

mentions.c: Afghanistan: Terrorist attack: 17 August 2019 Kabul bombing

Q113565637.label: killing of Darya Dugina
Q113565637.desc: car bombing which killed Daria Dugina, daughter of Alexander Dugin
Q113565637.summary: Darya Aleksandrovna Dugina, also known under the pen name Daria Platonova, was a Russian journalist, political scientist, and activist. She was the daughter of Aleksandr Dugin, a far-right political philosopher, whose political views and support for Vladimir Putin she shared.

Q126913477.label: 2024 Bolivian coup attempt
Q126913477.desc: military attempt to overthrow Luis Acre in La Paz
Q126913477.img: Intento de Golpe de Estado Bolivia 2024.jpg
Q126913477.summary: On 26 June 2024, an attempted military coup occurred in Bolivia, orchestrated by dissident officers of the Armed Forces led by General Juan José Zúñiga. Armed troops occupied the Plaza Murillo in La Paz, the political heart of the country, but withdrew amid domestic and international pressure and after the appointment of a new military high command.

Q48778693.label: Battle of Høljarast Bridge
Q48778693.summary: The Battle of Høljarast Bridge was a military engagement between Norwegian and German forces during the Norwegian Campaign. The battle ended with a partial Norwegian defeat as they were unable to hold their lines against German advance. Norwegians managed to withdraw in order destroying the strategic bridge so Germans would not be able to use it. Germans soon built an improvised bridge in the same place they named "Brandenburg".

Q29025221.label: Raid on Constanța
Q29025221.desc: Attack by the Soviet Black Sea Fleet on the Romanian port of Constanța in 1941
Q29025221.img: Romanian scout cruiser Mărăști at sea.jpg
Q29025221.summary: The Raid on Constanța was an attack by the Soviet Black Sea Fleet on the Romanian port of Constanța on 26 June 1941, shortly after the beginning of Operation Barbarossa, the Axis invasion of the Soviet Union, and resulted in the only encounter between major warships in the Black Sea during World War II. The attack was intended to be a coordinated effort between the fleet's ships and aircraft to split the attention of the defenders, but the bombers did not attack at the designated times.

Q250309.label: Battle of Tarawa
Q250309.desc: battle in the Pacific Theater of World War II, at the Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands
Q250309.summary: The Battle of Tarawa was fought on 20–23 November 1943 between the United States and Japan on Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands, now part of the Republic of Kiribati but then a Japanese-occupied British colony. The battle was part of Operation Galvanic, the U.S. invasion of the Gilberts, and ended in a decisive American victory. Nearly 6,400 Japanese, Koreans, and Americans died during the battle, mostly on and around the small island of Betio, in the extreme southwest of Tarawa Atoll. At the time, Betio was only 118 hectares.

Q124077509.label: Battle of Kosmach
Q124077509.summary: The Battle of Kosmach was fought between the 31st, 33rd, 87th Frontier Detachments, 256th Regiment of the NKVD in the Ministry of the Internal Affairs of the Soviet Union under the command of Aleksey Dergachev against the Armed Units “Skazheni”, “Hutsulskyi”, “Haydamaky” and “Pidkarpatskyi” of the 4th Operational Group “Hoverla” in the Western Operational Group of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army under the command of Myroslav Symsych and Pavlo Vatsyk in the Kosiv Raion of the Stanislav Oblast.

Q3883973.label: Operation Herring
Q3883973.img: Paracadutisti italiani salgono a bordo di un C-47 all'aeroporto di Rosignano (20 aprile 1945).jpg
Q3883973.summary: Operation Herring was the last World War II airborne combat drop in Europe.

Q7097797.label: Operations Malheur I and Malheur II
Q7097797.wiki: Operations Malheur I and Malheur II
Q7097797.img: Task Force Oregon Operational Area April - July 1967.jpg
Q7097797.summary: Operation Malheur I and Operation Malheur II were a series of search and destroy operations conducted by the 1st Brigade 101st Airborne Division operating as part of Task Force Oregon in Quảng Ngãi Province, South Vietnam.

Q16659909.label: Siege of Wadi Deif
Q16659909.desc: 2013 siege of two Syrian Army bases
Q16659909.summary: The siege of Wadi Deif was a siege of two Syrian Army bases, Wadi Deif and Hamadiyah, by rebel forces, starting on 11 October 2012, during the Idlib Governorate clashes of the Syrian civil war.

Q147909.label: Kingdom of Bulgaria
Q147909.desc: state on the Balkan Peninsula between 1908 and 1946
Q147909.summary: The Tsardom of Bulgaria, also known as the Third Bulgarian Tsardom, commonly known in English as the Kingdom of Bulgaria, or simply Bulgaria, was a constitutional monarchy in Southeastern Europe, which was established on 5 October [O.S. 22 September] 1908, when the Bulgarian state was raised from a principality to a tsardom.

Q150981.label: North German Confederation
Q150981.desc: historical federal state in today's Northern Germany (1867–1871)
Q150981.summary: The North German Confederation was a confederated state that united the region of Germany north of the Main river from July 1867 to December 1870. It was a milestone of German Unification that put the Kingdom of Prussia at the head of the emerging nation and led to the exclusion of Austria from the eventual united Germany.

Q244165.label: Republic of Artsakh
Q244165.desc: former de-facto state in South Caucasus from 1992 to 2023
Q244165.summary: Artsakh, officially the Republic of Artsakh or the Republic of Nagorno-Karabakh, was a breakaway state in the South Caucasus whose territory was internationally recognised as part of Azerbaijan. Between 1991 and 2023, Artsakh controlled parts of the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast of the Azerbaijani Soviet Socialist Republic, including its capital Stepanakert.

Q310213.label: Anton Graff
Q310213.summary: Anton Graff was a Swiss portrait artist.

Q965.label: Burkina Faso
Q965.summary: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa. It is bordered by Mali to the northwest, Niger to the northeast, Benin to the southeast, Togo and Ghana to the south, and Ivory Coast to the southwest. It covers an area of 274,223 km2 (105,878 sq mi). In 2024, the country had an estimated population of approximately 23,286,000. Its citizens are known as Burkinabes, and its capital and largest city is Ouagadougou.
